title: Uniquely normalized derived finite quotient transition
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes. Use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$, $S_{W,n}=(P_n)_W$, $B_W=\varprojlim_n S_{W,n}$, projections $\pi_{W,n}:B_W\to S_{W,n}$ and quotient maps $q_{W,b,a}:S_{W,b}\to S_{W,a}$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], for $W=T,T'$ and positive indices. Use completed-coefficient module pullback $G=g^*$ and its strict-tower version $G^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and the fixed finite interfaces of [def-cbc-completed-reduction-finite-interfaces].

Let $b\geq a\geq1$, and let $H_n(K)=Lg_n^*(K\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{T,n})$. For a cochain complex $P$ of $B_T$-modules write $P_n=P\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,n}$ and let $Q$ denote derived localization. Let
$$v_{n,P}:H_n(QP)\longrightarrow Q(g_n^*P_n)$$
be the canonical computation map formed from the universal derived scalar-extension counit and the exact finite pullback localization comparison (completedReductionFiniteModelMap in the fixed interface). These computation maps are natural in $P$, and are invertible on K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let
$$\delta_{b,a,P}:\operatorname{Res}_{q_{T',b,a}}Q(g_a^*P_a)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(\operatorname{Res}_{q_{T',b,a}}g_a^*P_a)$$
be the exact restriction/localization comparison. Let $t^0_{b,a}:g_b^*(-\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,b})\to\operatorname{Res}_{q_{T',b,a}}g_a^*(-\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,a})$ be the ordinary transformation specified on all inverse-image tensor generators in [lem-weil-pbc-ordinary-finite-evaluation-transition], and apply it termwise to $P$.

There exists a unique natural transformation
$$t_{b,a}:H_b\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{q_{T',b,a}}H_a$$
whose component on every K-flat $P$ satisfies the equality in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(S_{T',b}))$,
$$Q(t^0_{b,a}(P))\,v_{b,P}=\delta_{b,a,P}\,\operatorname{Res}_{q_{T',b,a}}(v_{a,P})\,t_{b,a}(QP).$$
This is precisely completedReductionTargetTransition with HasCompletedReductionTargetTransitionNormalization, rather than an arbitrarily chosen derived transition. The assertion concerns all derived inputs with no completeness, boundedness or flatness assumption on them, and includes equal indices. It does not assert that $S_{T',a}$ is flat over $S_{T',b}$, or that $t_{b,a}$ itself is invertible.

proof.text: First check the specified computation arrows. Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to the actual sheaf map $\pi_{T,n}:B_T\to S_{T,n}$. For K-flat $P$, its identity resolution computes scalar extension, so the universal counit $QP\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{T,n}\to QP_n$ is invertible. The finite coefficient ring $P_n$ is finite and discrete by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]; hence [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] applies to $g_n^*$. Its exact localization comparison is natural and invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The fixed $v_{n,P}$ is the image of that scalar counit followed by this exact comparison, as specified in [def-cbc-completed-reduction-finite-interfaces]. It is therefore natural in $P$ and invertible on K-flat $P$. Restriction of scalars does not change underlying abelian sheaves or their kernels and cokernels, so it is exact; the same exact-functor result supplies the natural isomorphism $\delta$ used in the statement.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(B_T)$ and $\mathcal P$ be the full subcategory of all K-flat cochain complexes. Every complex receives a quasi-isomorphism from an object of $\mathcal P$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], with no boundedness condition. Use the quotient $p:C(\mathcal A)\to K(\mathcal A)$: by the description of homotopy morphisms as complex maps modulo homotopy in [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], $p$ is full, surjective on objects and leaves objects unchanged. Set $\mathcal S\subset K(\mathcal A)$ to have the same K-flat objects, so $\mathcal P(P)$ iff $\mathcal S(pP)$. Taking the homotopy image of the resolution gives a quasi-isomorphism from $\mathcal S$ to every object of $K(\mathcal A)$. Quasi-isomorphisms there have the right calculus of fractions and localize to $D(\mathcal A)$ by [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated]. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-resolving-representative-whiskering] hold for $L=\mathcal P\hookrightarrow C(\mathcal A)\xrightarrow{Q}D(\mathcal A)$. Its conclusion gives full faithfulness of restriction along $L\times L$ into $\mathcal E=D(\operatorname{Mod}(S_{T',b}))$.

proof.text:
Put $J=\operatorname{Res}_{q_{T',b,a}}H_a$, $\alpha_P=v_{b,P}$ and $\beta_P=\delta_{b,a,P}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{q_{T',b,a}}(v_{a,P})$. These are natural transformations on cochain complexes, and $\beta_P$ is invertible on $\mathcal P$ by step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-ordinary-finite-evaluation-transition], $t^0_{b,a}$ is natural on module sheaves. Apply it in each degree. Its naturality for $d_P$ says precisely that the resulting maps commute with differentials; its naturality for a chain map gives naturality on complexes. Localizing yields $u_P=Q(t^0_{b,a}(P))$. Define, for $P\in\mathcal P$,
$$\theta_P=\beta_P^{-1}\circ u_P\circ\alpha_P:H_b(QP)\longrightarrow J(QP).$$
For a chain map $f:P\to P'$ between K-flat complexes, naturality of $\alpha,u,\beta$ gives
$$J(Qf)\theta_P=\beta_{P'}^{-1}u_{P'}\alpha_{P'}H_b(Qf)=\theta_{P'}H_b(Qf).$$
Thus $\theta$ is a natural transformation after restriction to $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Paragraph 1: termwise ordinary quotient map followed by localization; CompletedPullbackReduction.lean, completedReduction_descend_map and completedReduction_descend_composite, lines 793-869.

proof.text:
Use the full part of the restriction theorem [lem-weil-pbc-resolving-representative-whiskering] from step 2. On $\mathcal P\times\mathcal P$ the family $(P,R)\mapsto\theta_P$ is natural between the restrictions of $H_b\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$ and $J\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$, since these functors and this family ignore $R$. Lift it to a natural transformation $\Theta:H_b\circ\operatorname{pr}_1\to J\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$ on $D(\mathcal A)\times D(\mathcal A)$. Restrict $\Theta$ along the diagonal $K\mapsto(K,K)$ and call the resulting transformation $t:H_b\to J$. For every K-flat $P$ its component is $t(QP)=\Theta_{(QP,QP)}=\theta_P$. Hence
$$\beta_P\circ t(QP)=\beta_P\circ\beta_P^{-1}\circ u_P\circ\alpha_P=u_P\circ\alpha_P,$$
which is exactly the required normalization square. This uses the existing two-variable restriction theorem as stated; the diagonal turns its lift into the required one-variable transformation.

source.place: Paragraph 1: existence of the normalized derived transition; categories.tex Tag 04VK, applied via the existing resolving-representative theorem.

proof.text: If $t'$ is another natural transformation satisfying the displayed square, then for every K-flat $P$ its equation and that for $t$ give $\beta_P\circ t'(QP)=\beta_P\circ t(QP)$. Cancel the invertible $\beta_P$ to obtain $t'(QP)=t(QP)$. After precomposition by $\operatorname{pr}_1$ the two transformations agree on all $(QP,QR)$ with $P,R\in\mathcal P$. Faithfulness in [lem-weil-pbc-resolving-representative-whiskering] gives $t'\circ\operatorname{pr}_1=t\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$ on the derived product. Evaluating at $(K,K)$ for each $K$ gives $t'(K)=t(K)$, hence $t'=t$. The name completedReductionTargetTransition in [def-cbc-completed-reduction-finite-interfaces] denotes the descent with this normalization, so uniqueness identifies it with the transformation just constructed.

source.place: Paragraph 1: uniqueness of descent with the fixed K-flat equation; CompletedPullbackReduction.lean, lines 821-830 and 1518-1573.

proof.text: Every input to the construction was an arbitrary complex or derived object. Step 2 supplies K-flat representatives for all of them, so neither completeness, boundedness nor flatness of the input was introduced. Only the computation $\beta_P$ was inverted. The ordinary quotient formula and the argument apply for all $b\geq a\geq1$, including $b=a$, since quotient maps at equal indices are identities by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. No inverse of $t^0_{b,a}$ or $t_{b,a}$ and no flatness of $S_{T',a}$ over $S_{T',b}$ was used.

theorem completedReductionTargetTransition_exists (a b : ℕ) (h : a ≤ b) :
    ∃! τ : completedReductionFiniteTarget g d b ⟶
        completedReductionFiniteTarget g d a ⋙
          pbcDerivedRestrict (reductionCoefficientMap X d b a h),
      HasCompletedReductionTargetTransitionNormalization g d a b h τ
lean.note: Exact existing unique-existence theorem with the specified HasCompletedReductionTargetTransitionNormalization K-flat equation. The fixed completedReductionTargetTransition is precisely the chosen witness of this theorem. General AdicCoefficientDatum, arbitrary scheme morphism, all unbounded derived inputs, a <= b including equal indices; natural index i encodes positive exponent i+1. No new module or changes to the reviewed statement and proof.
